derivation.onset: Two assessments about 35 minutes apart on Day +4 disagree (ICE 9/10 vs 10/10; section 6.4). If the 9/10 counts, onset is Day +4 and the record (Day +5) is a 7.1 mismatch of +1 day; if the 10/10 counts, onset is Day +5 (ICE 8/10) and the record matches (7.7). The readings give different categories, so 7.5, reason conflicting assessments (section 7.5).
derivation.max_grade: Every reading gives Grade 1 as the highest (ICE 7-9; no other domain), equal to the record, so the same category 7.7 under both readings and 7.5 is not used (section 7.5, A23).

ambiguity_notes: Onset is 7.5 (conflicting assessments). Signed difference is not given as one number: +1 under the reading using the nursing ICE, 0 under the resident ICE. Documented_value lists both candidate dates but this is not a date range in the section 6.1 sense, so the 'inside the range' mismatch rule is not applied. Grade is unaffected by the conflict. Headache and acetaminophen on Day +6 are excluded; tocilizumab on Day +2 is not a competing cause (A35).
